---
title: "Modern Physics 2026-1"
---

Introduction to the fundamental concepts of modern physics, including special relativity, quantum phenomena, wave-particle duality, quantum mechanics, and atomic structure, with emphasis on conceptual understanding and mathematical foundations.

Course taught in Universidad EAFIT.

## Interesting Readings

- [1900–1925: The Breakdown of Physics, Prof. Roman Castañeda](readings/17+3297+carta+a+la+editora.pdf) — Historical overview of the scientific revolution that led to modern physics and quantum mechanics.

- [James Jeans’ Almost-Atomic Theory](readings/20-22-lighttouch%20(1).pdf) — A historical article discussing James Jeans’ early ideas about atomic structure before Bohr’s model.

- [The Quantum Theory of Radiation — Albert Einstein (1917)](readings/A.Einstein.pdf) — Einstein’s foundational paper introducing the concepts of spontaneous and stimulated emission.

- [On the Imaginable Content of Quantum Theoretical Kinematics and Mechanics — Werner Heisenberg (1927)](readings/Werner_Heisenberg_1927.pdf) — Original work presenting the uncertainty principle and the conceptual foundations of quantum mechanics.

- [The 1919 Measurement of the Deflection of Light](readings/will2015.pdf) — Historical review of the famous eclipse experiment that confirmed Einstein’s general relativity.

## Reference Textbook

The course follows the textbook *Modern Physics* (3rd Edition) by Raymond A. Serway, Clement J. Moses, and Curt A. Moyer as the main reference for lectures, derivations, and problem-solving activities.
